Numbers, rankings and counts are filled and validated by src/build_review_v2.py from output/step1. v1, v2 and v2.1 files are preserved unchanged.
author: claude-code-model-interpretation

patterns.title: The subs/signup step, not the cost of a signup, accounts for most of the cost/sub spread
patterns.observed: Cost/sub is an identity: cost per signup divided by subs per signup. Cost per signup sits in a narrow band for eight of nine terms ({t_free_cost_per_signup} to {t_vibe_cost_per_signup}; enterprise is the outlier at {t_enterprise_cost_per_signup}), while subs/signup ranges from {min_observed_sub_rate_pct} (free, github) to {max_observed_sub_rate_pct} (scaffold) and cost/sub from {t_scaffold_cost_per_sub} to {t_enterprise_cost_per_sub}. Direct comparison: free ({t_free_cost_per_signup}) and github ({t_github_cost_per_signup}) have the two cheapest signups in the sample but the two lowest subs/signup; scaffold and internal tools pay {t_scaffold_cost_per_signup} and {t_internal_cost_per_signup} per signup, close to the core term's {t_core_cost_per_signup}, and convert those signups at {t_scaffold_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} ({t_scaffold_paid_sub_per_signup_rank_high}) and {t_internal_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} ({t_internal_paid_sub_per_signup_rank_high}). Because the two factors are mathematically coupled, no correlation is reported; the decomposition itself is the evidence.
explanations: Intent mismatch: some queries bring people who register but were not going to pay (tutorial seekers, free seekers, developers looking for a repo).
Post-click mismatch: the landing page or onboarding does not serve those intents even though they could pay.
Lag: same-window subs undercount terms whose users take longer to convert; the ratio would rise with cohort-aligned data.
Signup definition: 'Regs' may include very low-commitment registrations for some traffic, inflating signups without intent.
Note for bidding: whichever explanation holds, cost per signup does not track cost/sub here; whether that matters depends on the account's current bidding event, which is unknown.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Cohort-aligned subs (60/90-day) separate lag from the rest; an FFT/activation event per term separates dead registrations from engaged ones; landing-page review and the matched keyword per row separate intent from post-click mismatch.

patterns.title: The sample splits into two performance tiers around the allowable, and the sample as a whole is above it
patterns.observed: Five terms below $181 account for {g_below_allowable_cost_share_pct} of sample cost and {g_below_allowable_sub_share_pct} of sample subs at {g_below_allowable_cost_per_sub}/sub (sub/signup {g_below_allowable_sub_rate_pct}). Four terms above $181 account for {g_above_allowable_cost_share_pct} of cost and {g_above_allowable_sub_share_pct} of subs at {g_above_allowable_cost_per_sub}/sub (sub/signup {g_above_allowable_sub_rate_pct}). The nine rows together run at {sample_cost_per_sub}/sub, above the allowable and above the scope benchmark {benchmark}; by subtraction, the unseen remainder of the scope runs at {remainder_cost_per_sub}.
explanations: Descriptive only: the split uses the same metric it groups by, so it is a summary, not an independent finding. Vibe coding ({t_vibe_ratio_to_allowable}) and how-to ({t_howto_ratio_to_allowable}) sit close to the boundary and could move across it with lag or small count changes.

The nine rows may be a curated 'hardest' subset of the scope rather than a representative slice: the remainder ({remainder_cost_per_sub}) is cheaper per sub than each of the three largest rows, including the core term ({t_core_cost_per_sub}).
The scope benchmark being below the allowable while the sample is above it means efficiency in the scope is carried by terms not shown.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: The full search-term report for the scope (the remaining ~35% of spend).

patterns.title: In this sample, the cheapest clicks convert worst; this is an observation, not a rule about price
patterns.observed: The three cheapest CPCs in the sample are github ({t_github_cpc}), free ({t_free_cpc}) and how-to ({t_howto_cpc}); together they are {g_cheapest_three_cpc_cost_share_pct} of sample cost, {g_cheapest_three_cpc_sub_share_pct} of subs, and convert signups at {g_cheapest_three_cpc_sub_rate_pct}. The most expensive click, enterprise ({t_enterprise_cpc}), converts at {t_enterprise_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}, {t_enterprise_paid_sub_per_signup_rank_low} in the sample. The observation therefore holds for the three cheap terms and fails for the most expensive one; it is not evidence that paying more per click buys better customers.
explanations: The three cheap terms share modifier words (free, github, how to) that may mark a non-buying stage; the low price and the low conversion could both follow from that, with neither causing the other.
Braid's landing pages may serve buying intents well and these intents poorly; cheap traffic is not inherently worse.
Enterprise's price is set by a different set of competitors; its low self-serve conversion may reflect a sales-led buyer rather than intent quality.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Landing-page review for the three cheap terms; whether enterprise visitors appear in a sales pipeline; the matched keyword and ad group for each row.

patterns.title: Sample-specific observation: use-case and competitor terms convert best here (hypothesis, not proof of value)
patterns.observed: The three use-case/competitor terms (no-code, internal tools, scaffold alternative) are {g_use_case_or_competitor_cost_share_pct} of sample cost but {g_use_case_or_competitor_sub_share_pct} of subs, at {g_use_case_or_competitor_cost_per_sub}/sub with subs/signup {g_use_case_or_competitor_sub_rate_pct}. The three terms built on the head phrase 'ai app builder' (core, free, github) are {g_head_plus_modifier_cost_share_pct} of cost and {g_head_plus_modifier_sub_share_pct} of subs at {g_head_plus_modifier_cost_per_sub}/sub; within that group the modifier separates them (core {t_core_cost_per_sub}, free {t_free_cost_per_sub}, github {t_github_cost_per_sub}). This is an observation about nine rows in one period: it says nothing about the value of the subscribers, their retention, or whether the ratio would hold at higher spend.
explanations: Specificity of buying intent: someone naming a use case or a competitor may have already decided to buy something (hypothesis).

Linguistic form is not the driver: 'vibe coding app builder' is head-plus-modifier and converts at {t_vibe_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}; 'enterprise app development platform' is use-case-shaped and converts at {t_enterprise_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}.
Volume effect: the use-case terms are small ({g_use_case_or_competitor_cost}); efficiency at this size does not imply efficiency at a larger size.
Customer value is unknown: a cheaper sub from a competitor query is not shown to be worth the same as a sub from the core term.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Impression share for the use-case terms (demand-limited or share-limited), existing keyword coverage, and retention or value by acquisition term if available.

patterns.title: Allowable-reach arithmetic: which above-allowable terms are within the range of conversion rates observed in the sample
patterns.observed: At current cost, meeting the $181 allowable would require: how-to {t_howto_subs_needed} subs ({t_howto_sub_rate_needed_pct} of its signups, {t_howto_subs_multiple_needed} its observed subs); free {t_free_subs_needed} subs ({t_free_sub_rate_needed_pct}, {t_free_subs_multiple_needed}); github {t_github_subs_needed} subs ({t_github_sub_rate_needed_pct}, {t_github_subs_multiple_needed}); enterprise {t_enterprise_subs_needed} subs ({t_enterprise_sub_rate_needed_pct}, {t_enterprise_subs_multiple_needed}). The highest subs/signup observed in the sample is {max_observed_sub_rate_pct}. Reaching the allowable is not financial break-even; the allowable is an operator target and its relation to margin is unknown.
explanations: How-to needs a rate ({t_howto_sub_rate_needed_pct}) that {t_howto_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} other sample terms already exceed; a lag or landing-page effect of that size is plausible.

Free and github need rates that {t_free_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} and {t_github_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} other terms reach, but {t_free_subs_multiple_needed} and {t_github_subs_multiple_needed} their own observed subs; lag alone would have to be large to close that.

Enterprise needs a rate above anything observed in this sample ({t_enterprise_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} terms exceed it). That is not impossible (enterprise buyers may behave unlike self-serve buyers, and the count is {t_enterprise_paid_sub} subs), but keeping the term under a Subs KPI at current cost means expecting a conversion rate no term here has shown. A lower cost per click or a different KPI (sales-assisted leads) would change the arithmetic.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Cohort-aligned conversion by term; whether an enterprise sales path exists and is tracked; the margin behind the allowable.

patterns.title: Signup rate does not separate good from bad terms; small counts limit two terms
patterns.observed: Signup/click runs from {t_enterprise_signup_per_click_pct} (enterprise) to {t_scaffold_signup_per_click_pct} (scaffold). 'free' has the {t_free_signup_per_click_rank_high} signup rate ({t_free_signup_per_click_pct}) and the {t_free_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high} cost/sub ({t_free_cost_per_sub}; enterprise {t_enterprise_cost_per_sub} and github {t_github_cost_per_sub} are higher). 'github' has a signup rate ({t_github_signup_per_click_pct}) close to how-to's ({t_howto_signup_per_click_pct}) and vibe's ({t_vibe_signup_per_click_pct}) yet the {t_github_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high} cost/sub. Two terms have very few subs (enterprise {t_enterprise_paid_sub}, github {t_github_paid_sub}), so their subs/signup rates are the least stable; no operator data-sufficiency threshold has been set.
explanations: A high signup rate on a 'free' query is expected regardless of intent to pay; signup rate measures the ease of registering, not the intent behind it.
For scaffold and internal tools, high signup rate and high subs/signup coincide, so signup rate is informative for buying-intent queries and misleading for others.
Small-count terms could look materially different with one more period of data.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Operator min_cost / min_subs thresholds; an FFT or activation event that separates engaged signups from registrations.

patterns.title: Match type shows no pattern and cannot be read as keyword structure
patterns.observed: Two rows are Phrase (core, free) and carry {g_phrase_rows_cost_share_pct} of sample cost at {g_phrase_rows_cost_per_sub}/sub; seven are Broad. Broad rows span the best ({t_scaffold_cost_per_sub}) and worst ({t_enterprise_cost_per_sub}) cost/sub. The column records the match type that triggered the search term, not the keyword or ad group behind it, and says nothing about how many queries sit in a row.
explanations: Each row is one search term as reported; which keyword matched it, in which ad group, and under which bidding strategy, is not in the data.
The two Phrase rows may come from one keyword or two; nothing in the data says which.
patterns.distinguishing_evidence: Matched keyword, ad group and campaign columns for each row (the standard search-term report fields), plus the bidding strategy per campaign.

observed_vs_explanations.observation: free: {t_free_signup} signups (most in sample), {t_free_paid_sub} subs, subs/signup {t_free_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}, cost/sub {t_free_cost_per_sub} ({t_free_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high})
observed_vs_explanations.explanations: no free tier and searchers leave; free tier exists and converts after a lag; landing page contradicts the 'free' promise
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: product fact on free tier; 90-day cohort conversion for this term; landing-page review

observed_vs_explanations.observation: github: cheapest CPC {t_github_cpc}, subs/signup {t_github_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}, {t_github_paid_sub} subs, cost/sub {t_github_cost_per_sub} ({t_github_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high})
observed_vs_explanations.explanations: developer audience not served; open-source seekers who never intended to buy; low count instability
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: product fact on GitHub/code export; ad and landing page for the query; another period of data

observed_vs_explanations.observation: enterprise: CPC {t_enterprise_cpc}, cost/signup {t_enterprise_cost_per_signup}, {t_enterprise_paid_sub} subs, cost/sub {t_enterprise_cost_per_sub} ({t_enterprise_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high}); needs {t_enterprise_sub_rate_needed_pct} subs/signup to reach $181, above the sample maximum {max_observed_sub_rate_pct}
observed_vs_explanations.explanations: enterprise buyers convert through sales, not self-serve; term is off-target; count too small to judge
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: whether a sales path exists and whether these signups appear as leads

observed_vs_explanations.explanations: tutorial seekers; slower conversion for learners; landing page not built for them
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: matched keyword for the row; cohort-aligned subs; a template/tutorial landing-page test

observed_vs_explanations.explanations: high buying intent; small terms not yet scaled; already isolated in the account; subscriber value unknown
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: impression share, existing keyword coverage, value or retention by acquisition term

observed_vs_explanations.explanations: sample is the hardest subset; period misalignment; different attribution
observed_vs_explanations.settling_evidence: full scope search-term report with dates

justified_now.action: Request the full scope search-term report with dates, matched keyword, ad group, campaign and bidding strategy
justified_now.why: P2 and P7: the sample is {sample_coverage_pct} of scope spend and {sample_sub_coverage_pct} of scope subs, runs above the allowable while the scope runs below it, and no row can be tied to a keyword or a bidding lever.

justified_now.action: Pull cohort-aligned (60/90-day) subs by search term and an FFT/activation event if one exists
justified_now.why: P1 and P6: the subs/signup step accounts for the spread; lag and dead registrations are the two explanations the data cannot separate.

justified_now.action: Review the ad and landing page served to the free, github, how-to and enterprise queries
justified_now.why: P1 and P3: intent mismatch and post-click mismatch produce the same numbers; this is the cheapest way to tell them apart and needs no account change.

justified_now.action: Pull impression share for the five below-allowable terms
justified_now.why: P4: efficient small terms are only expansion candidates if they are share-limited rather than demand-limited.

justified_now.action: Ask the operator for min_cost / min_subs thresholds and the margin behind the $181 allowable
justified_now.why: P5 and P6: two terms have {t_enterprise_paid_sub} and {t_github_paid_sub} subs, and 'reaching the allowable' cannot be read as break-even without the margin.

justified_now.action: Investigate whether the account optimises bidding to signups or cost per signup
justified_now.why: P1: cost per signup is nearly flat across terms whose cost/sub differs by more than ten times, so a signup-based target could favour the free and github queries. This is a concern to check, not a proven reason to change the bidding event: the current bidding setup, lag and usable signal volume are unknown.

requires_evidence.action: Any negative keyword (free, github, enterprise, how to)
requires_evidence.needs: the product fact named in the conditional recommendation for that term, the matched keyword/ad group, and what the negative would block in the remaining ~35% of scope
requires_evidence.why: the data shows low conversion, not irrelevance; a phrase negative also blocks unseen queries whose performance is unknown

requires_evidence.action: Bid or target changes on any term
requires_evidence.needs: the bidding strategy in use (manual, tCPA, tROAS, maximise conversions) and the keyword each term maps to
requires_evidence.why: under automated bidding, per-term bid advice is not executable; under tCPA the target, not the bid, is the lever

requires_evidence.action: New ad groups or keyword additions for use-case/competitor terms
requires_evidence.needs: existing keyword list and structure, impression share, and (for scaffold) trademark policy check
requires_evidence.why: they may already be isolated; adding a duplicate keyword changes nothing except internal competition

requires_evidence.needs: impression share / lost IS (budget vs rank) for its keyword
requires_evidence.why: below-allowable performance says nothing about headroom

requires_evidence.needs: whether a sales-assisted path exists and whether the {t_enterprise_signup} signups produced leads
requires_evidence.why: P5: no subs/signup rate seen in this sample would bring it to $181 at current cost, but that is the wrong test if the buyer converts through sales

v1_review.v1_statement: 'ai app builder' is 'the core/head keyword' and other rows are 'broad-match spillover'
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: The data has no keyword column; match type is the triggered type. Which keyword served each row, and whether the two Phrase rows share a keyword, is unknown.
v1_review.v2_position: Describe rows as search terms only; matched keyword and structure are requested inputs (P7).

v1_review.unsupported_assumption: A phrase negative blocks every query containing the word, including the unseen ~35% of scope spend and any query on other terms (e.g. a 'free' query that converts). Impact outside the nine rows is unknown; ad-group vs campaign scope is unknown.
v1_review.v2_position: Keep negatives conditional, and add the requirement to see what each would block in the full report before proposing a match type.

v1_review.v1_statement: 'Bid down', 'lower bid', 'capped bid' for free and how-to
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: Assumes manual or bid-cap control. The bidding strategy is unknown; under tCPA/maximise conversions there is no per-term bid to lower.
v1_review.v2_position: Replace with 'reduce exposure by the lever the bidding strategy allows' and list the strategy as a missing input.

v1_review.v1_statement: 'Isolate into its own ad group' for six terms
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: Assumes these terms are not already in dedicated ad groups and that the account is structured by intent. Structure is unknown; v1 did flag a coverage check but still framed isolation as the default action.
v1_review.v2_position: Coverage check is the action; isolation is one possible outcome of it.

v1_review.unsupported_assumption: 'Clear' overstates: {t_scaffold_paid_sub} subs on {t_scaffold_cost_share_pct} of spend with no impression share data. It is the best ratio in the sample; headroom is unknown.
v1_review.v2_position: Best-performing small term; expansion depends on impression share and existing competitor coverage.

v1_review.v1_statement: Enterprise: 'route to a demo/contact landing page'
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: Assumes an enterprise motion and a demo page exist.
v1_review.v2_position: P5: state the arithmetic (needs {t_enterprise_sub_rate_needed_pct} sub rate) and make the sales-path question the only decision input.

v1_review.v1_statement: 'Removing free leaves the rest at $159.17' presented as a useful scenario
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: Arithmetic is correct and was labelled as such, but it implicitly treats the term's spend as removable without affecting other rows or the unseen remainder.
v1_review.v2_position: Keep as arithmetic; do not use it to imply a post-negative cost/sub.

v1_review.unsupported_assumption: Judgement word on a channel comparison whose attribution basis is unknown.

v1_review.v1_statement: Least-certain term is 'free ai app builder'
v1_review.unsupported_assumption: A defensible judgement, but v1 did not show the alternative: how-to is the term closest to the allowable and the most likely to flip on lag or landing page alone (P5).
v1_review.v2_position: Present both candidates with the evidence that would resolve each; the operator picks.

least_certain.text: Two terms compete for 'least certain', for different reasons; the data does not rank them.

candidates.why: Largest swing: {t_free_cost_share_pct} of sample spend and the most signups. Needs {t_free_subs_multiple_needed} its observed subs to meet $181. The one piece of information: cohort-aligned free-to-paid conversion for this term (and whether a free tier exists at all).

candidates.term: how to build an ai app
candidates.why: Closest to the line: needs a subs/signup rate of {t_howto_sub_rate_needed_pct} against {t_howto_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} observed, a gap that lag or a landing-page change could close. The one piece of information: cohort-aligned subs/signup for this term after a tutorial/template landing-page test.

method_note: Cross-term patterns are computed over {term_count} rows in one period. Groups are arithmetic sums of the rows listed. Rank correlations from v2 are omitted: cost/sub equals cost per signup divided by subs per signup, so correlations among these metrics restate an identity and carry no causal information; the direct comparisons in P1 replace them. 'Subs needed at $181' is cost divided by the allowable, rounded up, at current cost: a statement of what reaching the operator's target would require, not a forecast and not financial break-even. No posture is chosen and the allowable is not adjusted. The methodology prior (bid on an early signal, judge on paid subs) is applied only as a caution in P1/P6: on this sample the early signals (signup rate, cost per signup) do not track paid subs, which is a reason to check the current bidding event, not a finding that it is wrong.
corrections: F1 ranking/count claims are computed placeholders, not hardcoded: enterprise subs/signup is {t_enterprise_paid_sub_per_signup_rank_low}; {t_howto_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} sample terms exceed how-to's required rate
F2 unknown product capability is not confirmed absence: github, free and enterprise negatives are pending confirmation of the named product fact
F3 signup-only optimisation is a concern to investigate, not a proven reason to change the bidding event; current bidding setup, lag and usable signal volume are unknown
table_note: 'Subs needed at $181' = ceil(cost / 181); 'sub rate needed' = that / signups. Arithmetic at current cost, not a forecast. Reaching the allowable is an operator target, not financial break-even: margin and customer value are unknown.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Largest above-allowable term ({t_free_cost_share_pct} of sample cost, {t_free_ratio_to_allowable}); needs {t_free_sub_rate_needed_pct} subs/signup vs {t_free_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} observed. Lean: reduce exposure before scaling anything else.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Keep and isolate instead if product confirms a free tier AND cohort-aligned (90-day) subs/signup for this term reaches about {t_free_sub_rate_needed_pct}. Negative candidate ('free', scoped to the matched keyword's ad group) only if product confirms there is no free tier, OR a free tier is confirmed and the cohort rate stays near {t_free_paid_sub_per_signup_pct}. Whether a free tier exists is currently unknown, so the negative is pending confirmation.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Same lean; redirect its budget to below-allowable terms with headroom rather than cutting overall spend.
conditional_recommendations.under_maintain_efficiency: Same lean, highest priority: it is the largest single contributor to the sample running above $181.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Cost/sub {t_github_cost_per_sub} is the {t_github_cost_per_sub_recomputed_rank_high} in the sample ({t_github_ratio_to_allowable}); needs {t_github_sub_rate_needed_pct} vs {t_github_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} observed on {t_github_paid_sub} subs. Lean: negative candidate ('github'), pending confirmation; whether Braid has a GitHub integration, code export or developer audience is unknown, and unknown is not absence.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Becomes an actionable negative only if product confirms there is no GitHub-related capability or developer audience. Becomes keep-and-test (developer landing page) if product confirms one exists. Hold judgement if the operator's min_subs threshold is above {t_github_paid_sub}.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Pending the product fact; if confirmed absent, negative; if confirmed present, landing-page test before any spend increase.
conditional_recommendations.under_maintain_efficiency: Pending the product fact; if confirmed absent, negative; if present, landing-page test first.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Highest cost/sub ({t_enterprise_cost_per_sub}); needs {t_enterprise_sub_rate_needed_pct} subs/signup, above the sample maximum {max_observed_sub_rate_pct}. Lean: stop judging it on self-serve subs.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: If a sales-assisted path is confirmed: move to lead-based measurement and a demo/contact page; the Subs comparison no longer applies. Negative candidate ('enterprise') only if product confirms there is no enterprise offering or sales path; that fact is unknown, so the negative is pending confirmation. If the operator's min_subs threshold is above {t_enterprise_paid_sub}: hold until more data.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Only with lead-based measurement in place.
conditional_recommendations.under_maintain_efficiency: Pending the product fact; negative if confirmed no enterprise path, otherwise measure on leads.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Above allowable ({t_howto_ratio_to_allowable}) but closest to it: needs {t_howto_sub_rate_needed_pct} vs {t_howto_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} observed, a rate {t_howto_n_terms_exceeding_needed_rate} sample terms exceed. Lean: keep, run a tutorial/template landing-page test before any negative.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Reduce exposure (by the lever the bidding strategy allows) if cohort-aligned subs/signup stays at or below {t_howto_paid_sub_per_signup_pct} after the landing-page test. Keep as is if cohort data alone lifts it to about {t_howto_sub_rate_needed_pct}.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Not a scaling candidate until it clears $181.
conditional_recommendations.under_maintain_efficiency: Second priority after free; landing-page test first because the gap is small.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Below allowable ({t_core_cost_per_sub}, {t_core_ratio_to_allowable}) with the most volume. Lean: keep.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Scale only if lost impression share (rank or budget) shows headroom for its keyword. Revisit if cohort-aligned cost/sub comes in above $181.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: First expansion candidate, conditional on headroom.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Below allowable ({t_nocode_cost_per_sub}) with {t_nocode_paid_sub} subs. Lean: keep.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Expand (dedicated keyword/ad group) if not already covered and impression share shows headroom. Nothing in the data turns it into a negative candidate.
Expand if not already covered, impression share shows headroom, and product confirms internal tools as a supported use case.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Lowest cost/sub ({t_scaffold_cost_per_sub}) on {t_scaffold_cost_share_pct} of cost. Lean: keep.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Expand (dedicated competitor ad group) if not already covered, impression share shows headroom, and competitor ad copy passes policy. Small size means expansion efficiency is unproven.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Below allowable ({t_vibe_cost_per_sub}, {t_vibe_ratio_to_allowable}) but near the scope benchmark. Lean: hold.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Reduce exposure if cohort-aligned cost/sub moves above $181; expand only if messaging fit is confirmed and headroom exists.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Secondary candidate after the core term.

conditional_recommendations.lean: Concern to investigate, not a conclusion: if the account currently optimises to signups or cost per signup, this sample suggests that signal would favour the free and github queries. The current bidding event, the signup-to-sub lag and the usable signal volume are unknown. In this analysis terms are judged on paid subs.
conditional_recommendations.flips_if: Confirm the current bidding event and strategy per campaign first. If bidding is already on subs or an activation event, no concern. If bidding is on signups, the next question is whether an FFT/activation event with enough volume tracks subs/signup across terms; only then is a change worth evaluating.
conditional_recommendations.under_scale: Same: investigate before any bidding-event change.

core.text: Core category intent: user wants a tool that builds AI apps. Closest match to the scope label itself; the matched keyword is unknown.

free.text: Price-sensitive or exploratory intent: wants to try without paying. Whether that is on-path depends entirely on whether Braid has a free tier and how long free->paid takes.

howto.text: Informational / learning intent; a share of searchers are looking for a tutorial rather than a product. Which keyword matched this term is unknown.

nocode.text: No-code builder intent. Efficient here, but whether Braid positions itself as no-code is unknown; if not, this may be an adjacent audience converting on a different promise.

vibe.text: Trend-driven intent ('vibe coding') for an AI-assisted builder. Likely aligned with the product category, but the phrase is new and its searcher mix may shift quickly.

enterprise.text: Enterprise buyer / evaluator intent. If Braid sells to enterprises via sales, these visitors would appear as leads, not self-serve subs, and cost/sub would not be the right KPI for this term. If Braid has no enterprise motion, the term is off-target.

internal.text: Use-case intent: build internal business tools. Converts well, which suggests the product serves this use case, but that is inferred from the data, not confirmed by product.

github.text: Developer intent: looking for an open-source repo, a GitHub-integrated builder, or code export. If Braid has no GitHub integration or does not target developers, this is off-target; if it does, the landing page may be failing this audience.

scaffold.text: Competitor-switching intent: Scaffold is the confirmed main competitor, so these are evaluators comparing alternatives. High readiness to buy is consistent with the ratios.
